title: Practice: Indicators of a Chemical Reaction
description: A short practice set on five common indicators of chemical reactions and the difference between chemical and physical changes.

questions.question: Which observation is the best evidence that a chemical reaction may have happened?
options: A piece of paper is folded in half.
A new solid forms when two clear liquids are mixed.
questions.explanation: A new solid forming from two liquids is called a precipitate. It is a common indicator that a new substance may have formed.

questions.question: Which list contains only common indicators of a chemical reaction?
options: Color change, gas release, precipitate formation, odor production, temperature change
Size change, shape change, location change, speed change, sound change
questions.explanation: The five common indicators are color change, formation of a precipitate, release of gas, production of odor, and a temperature change.

questions.question: True or False: Bubbles always prove that a chemical reaction has occurred.
questions.explanation: Boiling water forms bubbles, but it is a physical change. Bubbles are stronger evidence when they are not caused by boiling and represent a new gas product.

questions.question: Melting ice is best classified as a physical change because
questions.explanation: Melting changes the state from solid to liquid, but the substance remains water. No new substance forms.

questions.question: A solid that forms when two solutions are mixed is called a ________.
questions.explanation: A precipitate is an insoluble solid that forms during some chemical reactions in solution.

questions.question: A sliced apple slowly turns brown after being exposed to air. Which indicator is most obvious?
questions.explanation: The browning of a sliced apple is an observable color change caused by chemical reactions with oxygen in the air.

questions.question: True or False: A chemical change forms one or more new substances.
questions.explanation: This is the central idea of a chemical change: reactants are changed into products with new properties.

questions.question: A student says, "Boiling water is a chemical reaction because bubbles appear." In one or two sentences, explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: Boiling water is a physical change because liquid water becomes water vapor, which is still water. Bubbles alone do not prove a chemical reaction.
questions.explanation: The key correction is that bubbles can come from a change of state. A chemical reaction requires evidence that a new substance formed.
